approach: Treat the released repository as the source of truth: set up Python 3.12, install the dependency set (trying the pinned requirements first and relaxing only if they cannot resolve), then run the authors' single experiment script as released. A thin reproduce.py will invoke scripts/trimcal_eval.py --skip-compile, read the regenerated data/main_results.csv, filter to noisy cells, aggregate Gated-LWCal ECE with equal weight per noisy cell, and write results/metrics.json. The quick mode will be used only as a smoke test, and the full run will provide C1 plus cheap cross-checks for C2-C8. No author code is modified; any version-induced drift is logged in the metrics file.

files.purpose: Existing author experiment script; run as-is with --skip-compile. It generates the 432 noisy random-forest cells, calibrators, CSVs, and figures.
Optional relaxed dependency lock used only if the authors' pinned requirements.txt cannot resolve on Python 3.12. Keeps the environment reproducible without changing author code.
Thin wrapper: runs the author script, loads data/main_results.csv, computes the noisy-cell aggregate for Gated-LWCal ECE, cross-checks related Table III/V values, and writes results/metrics.json.

config.skip_latex_compile: true (paper artifact notes; avoids optional LaTeX dependency)

dependency_install.note: Relax pins only if the author-pinned versions are unavailable on Python 3.12; log installed versions.

base_model.random_state: cell seed from fixed seed list (A10)

datasets.binarization: one-vs-rest for named classes; Digits High = digit>=5; Digits Even = parity even (A11)
datasets.synthetic_generators: matched to Table II n/d/positive-rate with low class_sep, many irrelevant features, or class imbalance by task (A12)

split.test_labels: clean and used only for evaluation (R14)

config.seeds: 0..5 shared across split, RF, noise, and bootstrap RNGs (A2)

noise.modes: symmetric and asymmetric noisy calibration cells (paper Table V)
noise.asymmetric_rates: positive flip eta, negative flip eta/2 (A3)

calibration.gate_statistic: d_hat = fraction of calibration points where base 0.5 decision disagrees with noisy label (R7)

aggregate.paired_bootstrap: 2000 percentile paired resamples over matched dataset/seed/noise-mode/noise-rate cells, fixed seed 0 (R11/A13)

steps: Clone https://github.com/ZemingL/lwcal if the repository is not already present, cd to the repo root, and confirm scripts/trimcal_eval.py, data/main_results.csv, and requirements.txt exist.

Create a Python 3.12 virtual environment and install dependencies. First run pip install -r requirements.txt; if the pinned versions do not resolve, install requirements-repro.txt with relaxed bounds and record the actual versions.
Inspect scripts/trimcal_eval.py enough to confirm the RF settings are n_estimators=160, min_samples_leaf=2, max_features='sqrt', and that the script writes data/main_results.csv and main_summary.csv.
Run the smoke command: python scripts/trimcal_eval.py --quick --skip-compile. Confirm it exits 0, updates data/main_results.csv, and contains Gated-LWCal rows.
Inspect data/main_results.csv headers and unique values for method/calibrator, noise_rate/eta, noise_mode, and dataset. Map column aliases robustly; do not alter author code.

Write reproduce.py as a thin wrapper. It must resolve the repo root from __file__, run [sys.executable, 'scripts/trimcal_eval.py', '--skip-compile'] with cwd=repo root and a timeout, then read data/main_results.csv.

In reproduce.py, normalize method names and select Gated-LWCal aliases. Filter to noisy cells with eta/noise_rate > 0. Verify the selected Gated-LWCal row count is 432; if not, stop and report the mismatch rather than silently aggregating.

Compute the equal-cell mean ECE, NLL, and Brier for Gated-LWCal; also compute Raw, Isotonic, and LWCal ECE/NLL aggregates for cross-checks. Compute a paired bootstrap 95% interval for Gated-LWCal vs Raw ECE over matched cells if compatible columns exist.

Write results/metrics.json with primary_claim=C1, value, target=0.122, tolerance_abs=0.02, pass flag, n_cells, command, git commit if available, installed package versions, and cross-check values for C2-C8.

Run python reproduce.py end-to-end. Confirm C1 passes if abs(value - 0.122) <= 0.02; if not, inspect filtering, method aliases, eta column, and whether the script wrote a different table version before changing anything.
Keep author code unmodified. If dependency relaxation changes results beyond tolerance, report the version delta and the regenerated CSV paths in results/metrics.json.
smoke_test: python scripts/trimcal_eval.py --quick --skip-compile (expected ~10 seconds). After it finishes, assert data/main_results.csv exists and has at least one Gated-LWCal row; compute a mean ECE on that small nonempty subset to prove the CSV-to-metric path works before the full run.
intermediate_checks: Confirm 9 dataset names appear in data/dataset_summary.csv or equivalent output and inspect positive rates/class balance for plausibility.
Confirm the full noisy-cell universe after filtering eta>0 contains 432 Gated-LWCal rows; if rows are long-format over methods, check 432 cells times the number of methods instead.
Check that method aliases include Gated-LWCal and LWCal and that Raw/Isotonic/Platt/Beta rows are also present for cross-checks.
Inspect scripts/trimcal_eval.py for RF hyperparameters: 160 trees, min_samples_leaf=2, max_features='sqrt'.
Check that d_hat, rho, m, s, and calibration weights are present in logs/CSVs; if the author script logs them elsewhere, point reproduce.py at those files instead of recomputing.
Run the quick smoke before the full run and verify data/main_results.csv is nonempty and parseable by pandas.
Before accepting the full result, compute raw RF ECE and isotonic ECE from the same regenerated CSV; expect values near 0.188 and 0.147 respectively.
Check for NaNs/infinities in ECE, NLL, and Brier columns before aggregation; enforce NLL clipping only in the wrapper if needed for cross-checks.
Confirm that eta=0/clean rows are excluded from the headline aggregate and that equal-cell weighting is used, not dataset-balanced weighting.
Confirm results/metrics.json is valid JSON and contains the exact command, row count, target, tolerance, and pass/fail boolean for C1.
budget_plan: Total ~30 minutes on CPU. 0-5 min: clone/inspect repo and confirm the author script. 5-12 min: create venv and install dependencies, relaxing pins only if necessary. 12-14 min: run the --quick smoke and inspect CSV schema. 14-26 min: run the full --skip-compile experiment. 26-30 min: aggregate, write results/metrics.json, validate C1 and cross-checks, and leave buffer for dependency/version surprises.
